policy_tie_convention: Existing forgetting rule: product 2 iff advantage > 1e-6; product 1 at numerical ties. Saved OE-p0 mixtures remain the competition policy. Matched-mixture monopoly is sensitivity only, without extra simulations.

definitions.policy: P(product 2 | own seller selected, own reputation x).
definitions.product2_conditional: Stationary: product 2 fraction of own sales. Simulation: total product 2 sales / total own sales across independent paths (pooled ratio); competition pools both symmetric sellers.
definitions.product2_calendar: Product 2 sales per calendar period for one seller; competition averages A and B.
definitions.seller_profit: Profit per calendar period for one seller, including zero-profit periods when the outside option or rival sells; competition averages A and B.
definitions.sale_rate: Probability the seller makes a sale in a calendar period; competition pools symmetric sellers and equals 1/2.
definitions.conditional_uncertainty: 95% Student-t interval using independent-path cluster delta-method SE for the pooled ratio; zero-sale paths remain in the cluster sample; entire zero-sale samples are unavailable.
definitions.other_uncertainty: 95% Student-t intervals across 20 independent path means; all MC intervals exclude initialization bias.
definitions.finite_window_expected: Exact finite-grid expected outcomes over retained periods from initial reputation .5 after burn-in; conditional usage is ratio of expected sale counts, the pooled estimator target.
definitions.stationary_usage_identity: Only the matched-mixture sensitivity shares the competition own-sale event chain; its stationary conditional product-2 share equals competition. The main forgetting curve uses its original pure tie rule.
definitions.scope: Finite common 51-point grid, stationary and finite-window outcomes; saved OE-p0 competition is not asserted to be a full-state Markov-perfect equilibrium.
